st: Heat [[0.5 cup]] of the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and fry the sliced onions, stirring often, for 20 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Lift them out onto paper towels and salt them, keeping the oil in the pan.
Boil the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until just tender, then drain and set aside.
In a pot, heat [[2 tbsp]] of the reserved onion oil, add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Add [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until tender, then drain well.

For the tomato sauce, fry the garlic in [[2 tbsp]] of the remaining oil for 30 seconds. Add the crushed tomatoes, [[1.5 tsp]] cumin, the cayenne and [[1 tsp]] salt, then simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Make the vinegar sauce by mixing [[2 tbsp]] vinegar with [[0.25 cup]] water, [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and a pinch of salt.
Warm the chickpeas in a small pan with a splash of water and a pinch of salt for 3 minutes.
Layer rice, lentils and pasta in each bowl. Top with chickpeas, a ladle of tomato sauce and a spoonful of vinegar sauce.
Finish with a big handful of crispy onions and a drizzle of the last [[1 tbsp]] vinegar if you like it tangy.
Pour the fava beans and their liquid into a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Simmer for 10 minutes so the flavors soak in. Stir now and then so the beans do not catch on the bottom.
Mash about half of the beans roughly with a fork or potato masher right in the pot, leaving the rest whole for texture.
In a small bowl, mix the garlic, cumin, the juice of both lemons and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Stir the garlic mixture into the beans and cook 3 more minutes. Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Spoon the beans into a shallow bowl and drizzle with [[3 tbsp]] olive oil and the tahini if using.
Top with the tomato, parsley and a pinch of chili flakes, and finish with the last [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Serve hot with warm pita or flatbread for scooping.
Drain the soaked fava beans very well and pat them dry. They must be soaked but never cooked.
Put the beans, parsley, cilantro, onion and garlic in a food processor and pulse until the mixture looks like coarse, bright green crumbs.
Add the cumin, coriander, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda, then pulse once or twice to combine. It should hold together when squeezed.
Chill the mixture for 20 minutes so it firms up.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into flat patties about 2 inches wide. Press sesame seeds onto both sides, using [[0.25 cup]] in total.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Test with a pinch of mix, which should sizzle right away.
Fry 4 or 5 patties at a time for 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot in pita with tahini sauce, tomato and pickles.

ing: thawed; or fresh leaves finely chopped
st: Put the chicken, onion half, bay leaf and a good pinch of salt in a pot with [[6 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and simmer 35 minutes.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate and strain the broth. Measure [[5 cups]] of broth back into the pot.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and stir in the thawed molokhia. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Do not let it boil hard.
In a small pan, melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic with the coriander for about 1 minute until fragrant and just golden.
Pour the sizzling garlic mixture into the soup. It will hiss. Stir well and simmer 3 more minutes, then season with salt.
Meanwhile, brown the chicken pieces under a hot broiler for 5 minutes per side so the skin side is crisp, and check that they reach 165°F (74°C).
Serve the soup in bowls over rice with the chicken on top.
Trim the zucchini and use a small spoon or corer to scoop out the insides, leaving walls about 1/4 inch thick. Keep the vegetables upright when you are done.
In a large bowl, mix the rice, grated onion, parsley, dill, garlic, cumin, [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[0.5 cup]] crushed tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Spoon the filling into each vegetable until about three-quarters full, since the rice will swell as it cooks.
Stand the vegetables snugly in a wide pot. Put the pepper tops back on.
Stir the rest of the crushed tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tbsp]] oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 cups]] water together and pour it around the vegetables.
Set a heavy plate on top to keep them from floating. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 50 minutes.
Check that the rice is tender. If not, simmer 10 more minutes, adding a splash of water if the pot looks dry.
Let stand 10 minutes, then serve warm with some of the cooking sauce spooned over.
Put the lamb, onion, bay leaf, cinnamon stick and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes until the lamb is very tender. Lift out the meat and keep [[2 cups]] of the broth.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the torn pita with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and bake 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
For the tomato sauce, cook half the garlic in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 30 seconds, add the crushed tomatoes and [[1 tsp]] salt, and simmer 10 minutes.
For the garlic vinegar sauce, fry the remaining garlic with the coriander in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 1 minute, then pour in the vinegar and cook 1 minute.
In a deep serving dish, layer the toasted pita and soak it with about [[1 cup]] of warm broth.
Spread the rice over the bread, then drizzle with the tomato sauce and the garlic vinegar sauce.
Arrange the lamb on top, moisten with a little more broth, and serve right away while the bread is still a bit crisp.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet.
In a bowl, mix the beef with the onion, bell pepper, chili, parsley, cumin, paprika, black pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt until evenly combined.
Cut each pita open along one edge to make a pocket, or split it in half if it is thin.
Stuff about a quarter of the meat into each pita and press it flat and even all the way to the edges.
Brush the outsides with the melted butter and set them on the baking sheet.
Bake for 20 minutes, flip, and bake another 10 minutes until the bread is crisp and the meat is cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Rest 3 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve with tahini sauce or yogurt.
If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water for 20 minutes so they do not burn.
In a large bowl, combine both meats with the onion, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Knead the mixture with your hands for 2 minutes until sticky and well mixed. This helps it hold on the skewer.
Cover and chill for 15 minutes to firm up.
Wet your hands, divide the meat into 8 portions, and mold each one around a skewer into a long sausage shape about 5 inches long.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the kofta for 3 to 4 minutes per side, turning until browned all over and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with pita, tahini sauce and sliced tomato and onion.
Mix the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and milk and knead for 10 minutes into a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, coat each with a little oil, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Oil your work surface. Stretch one ball out as thin as you can, until you can almost see through it, pulling gently with oiled hands.
Brush the sheet with melted ghee and dab with a little softened butter, then fold it into thirds like a letter, and fold again into a small square.
Place the folded squares on a tray, cover, and rest 30 more minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Stretch each square gently into a flat 8-inch round and brush the top with melted ghee.
Bake for 15 minutes until puffed, flaky and golden brown.
Brush with more ghee while warm and serve with honey drizzled on top.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the puff pastry on a sheet for 20 minutes until deep golden, then let cool.
Break the cooled pastry into rough bite-sized pieces and spread half in a baking dish about 8 inches square.
Scatter half the raisins, nuts and coconut over the pastry, then add the rest of the pastry and the remaining toppings.
Warm the milk, [[0.5 cup]] cream, the sugar and vanilla in a pan until the sugar dissolves and it is steaming but not boiling.
Pour the hot milk evenly over the pastry so it is moistened all the way through.
Whip the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cream to soft peaks and spoon it on top.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15 minutes until the top is bubbling and browned in spots.
Dust with cinnamon and serve warm in bowls.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9 by 13 inch baking pan.
In a bowl, mix the semolina, coconut, [[0.75 cup]] sugar and baking powder.
Stir in the yogurt and melted butter until you have a thick, even batter. Let it rest 10 minutes so the semolina can soak.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan with a wet spatula and cut it into diamonds with a knife before baking.
Press an almond into the center of each diamond.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden brown on top.
While it bakes, boil the syrup: simmer [[1.5 cup]] sugar with [[1 cup]] water for 8 minutes, then stir in the juice of the lemon and cool.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake right out of the oven, let it soak in for 20 minutes, then serve.
Stir the jar of tahini very well, since the oil separates and settles on top.
Put the tahini in a bowl and add the lemon juice. The mixture will seize up and become thick, which is normal.
Add the garlic, cumin and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Whisk in the cold water a splash at a time until the sauce turns pale and creamy.
Keep adding water until it is the thickness of heavy cream, using up to [[0.33 cup]] in total.
Taste and add more salt or lemon if needed, then sprinkle with the parsley.
Whisk yeast and sugar into the warm water and rest 5 minutes until foamy.
Add both flours and salt, mix and knead for 10 minutes until soft and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 60 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each into a 7 inch round about 1/4 inch thick. Press both sides into the bran.
Rest the rounds on a floured towel for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 500°F with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Bake the rounds 4 minutes until puffed into a balloon and lightly browned. Cool slightly and split to fill.
nt: Baked at 500°F on a hot stone
Best swap: no bran, use extra whole wheat flour or cornmeal for dusting, same amount.

st: Whisk the flour, semolina, yeast, baking powder and [[2 cups]] warm water into a thin pourable batter. Rest 30 minutes.
Boil [[1 cup]] sugar with [[0.5 cup]] water for 8 minutes, add [[1 tsp]] lemon juice and cool. This is the syrup.
Mix the walnuts with [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] cinnamon for the filling.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. Pour 3 tablespoons of batter to make a 3 inch pancake. Cook only one side, 2 minutes, until bubbles pop and the top looks dry.
Cool the pancakes. Put a spoonful of filling on the cooked side, fold into a half moon and pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry the qatayef 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain, then dip in the cold syrup and serve.
nt: Pan cooked on one side, stuffed and deep fried
Best swap: bake the sealed qatayef at 375°F for 15 minutes brushed with melted butter, instead of frying. Pistachio works in place of walnuts.

st: Whisk [[3 tbsp]] cornstarch into [[0.5 cup]] cold milk in a small bowl until smooth with no lumps.
Pour the remaining milk into a saucepan and add [[3 tbsp]] sugar. Heat over medium until steaming.
Slowly whisk in the cornstarch mixture. Keep whisking over medium-low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the drink thickens like a loose custard.
Remove from heat and stir in [[1 tsp]] rose water.
Pour into warm mugs and top with the coconut, pistachios and a dusting of cinnamon. Serve at once, with a spoon.
nt: Thickened on the stovetop while whisking
Best swap: real sahlab powder from orchid root can replace the cornstarch at 2 tablespoons; dairy-free use oat milk.

st: Peel the cane stalks and cut them into 3 inch pieces, then split each piece into thin strips so they fit the press.
Chill the glasses in the freezer while you work so the juice stays cold and frothy when poured.
Press the strips through a sugarcane or masticating juicer. If using ginger, feed it through with the cane.
Squeeze the lemon into the juice and stir. The acid cuts the sweetness and keeps the green color.
Fill glasses with ice, pour in the juice, and serve immediately while it is frothy and cold.
nt: No cook: press cane with lemon, serve over ice
Best swap: no juicer, blend cane strips with 1 cup water and strain through muslin; or use bottled cane juice.
